scope: Four finite ABBA host/GPU/GPU/host replays of frozen round40 from checkpoint39; no games or promoted checkpoints.

tolerances.packed_arrays: bitwise identical including shapes, dtypes and order
tolerances.guard_decisions: exact for adoption; otherwise diagnose and leave opt-in

passive_memory.interpretation: Linux passive counters. Swap and PSI are system-wide and may include unrelated work; Windows host paging is not measured. Peak RSS is a process lifetime high-water mark that includes model loading/compilation and mapped pages, not incremental cache RAM. Sampled update RSS is also total resident process memory, not additional cache RAM.

passive_gpu.interpretation: Sampled busy/activity percentage, not FLOPS, occupancy or available compute capacity. VRAM includes TensorFlow allocator retention and other GPU users, not just logical input payloads.

primary_timing_rule: Compare only identical work counts AND exact guard accepted/reason sequence AND exact final PCG. Retain every timing/retry outcome; do not pool unmatched work.
limitations: One frozen saved round on one GPU measures update runtime, not learning strength or production training throughput.
GPU activity percentage is sampled busy time, not FLOPS, SM occupancy or available compute capacity.

The device-cache cap counts logical tensor payload bytes, not TensorFlow allocator overhead, activations, gradients, model weights or total VRAM. Retained allocator memory may remain after cache cleanup.
GPU inputs remain frozen for this one update; model outputs, KL and losses are recomputed after every proposal. No quantization or model/RL settings changed.
GPU floating-point execution can vary in unchanged A/A controls. Different retry/work or guard sequences remain separate from primary timing comparisons.
Initial model, both Adam-array digests, PCG, full config and input hashes match exactly. Final GPU arrays need not be bitwise equal; every pair is checked against predeclared envelopes.
No GPU trace was recorded. NVIDIA samples measure activity/VRAM, not the count or duration of individual transfers.
Linux memory/PSI/swap counters are passive; system-wide counters may include unrelated activity and do not measure Windows host paging.
Peak RSS includes model loading/compilation, Python/TensorFlow overhead and mapped pages; it is not incremental cache RAM. OS page cache can add reclaimable memory outside RSS.
Resident game-generation workers are absent. Production end-to-end memory pressure and performance remain unmeasured.
Full update timing includes initial rollout scan, prepacking, once-only cache upload, PPO work and cleanup. Model restore and graph compilation occur before the timed interval.
Source-file OS caches can be warmer in later runs. ABBA order mitigates a simple monotonic drift but four trials do not provide a robust speedup confidence interval.
Legacy host reports predate device-only telemetry. Their missing device fields are reported as absent; no device-resident cache was active.
NVIDIA wall timestamps have 5–6 backward adjustments per replay, at most 0.768s. GPU activity curves/window alignment are approximate; monotonic update timings are unaffected.

adoption.full_update_parity: within declared limits; matching-work guard decisions and final PCG exact
adoption.runtime_rule: Use fresh pinned deployment, never patch a running study. Production memory/throughput still unmeasured.

passive_gpu_wall_clock_caveat: NVIDIA wall timestamps have 5–6 backward adjustments per replay, at most 0.768s. GPU activity curves/window alignment are approximate; monotonic update timings are unaffected.
